_readme: Card panels whose highlight is a region grown on the parent bone, not the
atlas object the mapping names. Read by renderMusclePanels.py --regions.
Rules are landmarkRegions.py rules (same kinds as landmark-regions.rules.json);

rule._why: The lateral malleolus is the distal end of the fibula. The atlas's own 'Lateral malleolus' object is a flat marker disc beside the bone.
The medial malleolus is the process of the tibia that hangs below the plafond; the lowest slab of the tibia is it.

The posterior end of the calcaneus, where the Achilles tendon inserts. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The blade of C7's spinous process, the posterior 20mm (the lumbar spinous-process rule measured 18mm). Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The forked tips of the cervical spinous processes, C2 to C6 (the atlas names C2 'Axis (C2)'; 'Vertebra C2' matched nothing and C2 went unpainted until the owner spotted it) (owner: the other cervical vertebrae have one too; C7's is usually single and long, its own landmark). The posterior 12mm of each. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The notch in the upper border of the manubrium, between the clavicular notches: the top 12mm, central 22mm only (8mm by 15mm was too small to see at a whole-chest framing). Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The medial tuberosity of the navicular: the whole bone, cut to its medial 12mm (the medial-malleolus trick). Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The proximal (posterior) 15mm of the fifth metatarsal, with its tuberosity. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The proximal 12mm of the first metacarpal, at the saddle joint with the trapezium. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The distal 12mm of the first metacarpal; the landmark route's rule aims at an anchor the panel route does not have. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The hook projects palmarward (anterior, palms forward): the most palmar 7mm of the hamate. Added 18 Oct 2026 for the Atlas card; the spec's anchor sits off the bone (renders/landmarks-render.log), so the region is grown on the bone instead.

The tubercle is the scaphoid's palmar, distal, radial prominence: the bone's extreme in that direction on the left hand, mirrored for the right. The atlas's 'Tubercle of scaphoid bone.j' label, snapped to the bone, lands within about 3mm of it. A palmar slab (the first two tries) marked a sliver that wrapped onto the dorsum. Added 19 Oct 2026; point measured in world millimetres with probe_last4.py (+x body left, +y posterior, +z up).

SECOND PASS. Owner: the hit zone was a bone, not the space between the tendons and the end of the radius. The snuffbox is the hollow bounded by extensor pollicis longus (dorsal/ulnar), extensor pollicis brevis (palmar/radial; abductor pollicis longus beside it) and, above, the end of the radius; its floor is the scaphoid and trapezium. MEASURED (probe_snuff.py, left wrist, world mm): tendon centrelines at z 857, 849.7 and 845; radius ends at z 856. The highlight is the floor that shows through that outline, looked into from its outward direction (lateral-dorsal, +x+y on the left hand). The three tendons are drawn in red (--context). Left hand only: the panels show the left.

The inferior articular processes hang down behind the body, either side of the spinous process: L4's lowest points more than 10mm from the midline and 15mm behind its centre, both sides. The atlas has no anchor for them. Added 19 Oct 2026; point measured in world millimetres with probe_last4.py (+x body left, +y posterior, +z up).

transverse-ligament-of-atlas._why: Not in the atlas. A band from the medial surface of one lateral mass of C1 to the other, arching behind the dens: the lateral masses' medial surfaces at the dens's depth are (+-8.2, 8.5, 1541.9); the back of the dens at mid-height is y 15.3, so the band passes 2.5mm behind it. Added 19 Oct 2026 (owner: build them from measured points; probe_atlas.py / probe_atlas2.py, world mm).

alar-ligaments._why: Not in the atlas. Two cords from the sides of the dens tip (+-4.7, 9.3, 1547.7) up and out to the medial faces of the occipital condyles (+-8.8, 9.8, 1555.5), the condyles being the occipital surface that sits on C1's superior facets. Added 19 Oct 2026 (owner: build them from measured points; probe_atlas.py / probe_atlas2.py, world mm).

patellar-ligament._why: The atlas has only the ligament's two attachment patches (.o on the patella's apex, .e on the tibial tuberosity); the ligament is the solid spanning them. The right knee only: a hull over both knees' patches spans the gap between the legs. Added 19 Oct 2026 (owner: build them from measured points; probe_atlas.py / probe_atlas2.py, world mm).

triangular-fibrocartilage-complex._why: Owner's reference (dorsal view): the complex lies in the gap between the ulnar head (with the radius's ulnar edge) above and the lunate and triquetrum below. FOURTH PASS (owner: still passing through bones). Built as a gap fill: over the footprint, a vertical line through each point meets the ulna/radius under-surface and the lunate/triquetrum upper surface, and the solid is what lies between (gaps up to 10mm). Its top and bottom ARE those bone surfaces, so it touches both and goes through neither. Footprint (world mm, left wrist): from the ulnar styloid (243.4,-11.1) across to the radius's ulnar edge (257, -6.5 to -25) and back along the triquetrum (241,-26). Earlier passes (a hull through measured corners, then cut by the bones) wrapped round the ulnar head. FIFTH PASS (owner: 'too geometric'). Re-meshed and smoothed, inflated 0.4mm so it still meets the bones, then cut back by the four bones (build.smooth, build.subtract). SIXTH PASS (owner: now too small). Inflated 1.6mm after smoothing (the bone cut trims anything that enters a bone, so only the outer walls grow), the footprint widened 1-1.5mm, and the strip under the radius kept as well as the ulnar piece (build.keepPieces). SEVENTH PASS, from the owner's reference plate (dorsal view): the complex shown as fibre bundles fanning over the back of the joint from the ulnar head and styloid base to the triquetrum and lunate, over the disc. Five 1.8mm bundles between measured dorsal-surface points (probe_tfcc4.py): ulnar head (241.8..248.6, -6.2..-9.1, 860..864) to triquetrum (240.5..245.6, -12.9..-17, 849..851.5) and lunate (250.5..252.1, -10..-11.5, 855..856), each bowed 1.5mm dorsally so it lies on, not in, the bones; then cut by the bones. EIGHTH PASS (owner: add the palmar parts from the wrist slide, elbow deck p24): palmar ulnolunate and ulnotriquetral fibres from the front of the ulnar head and disc to the palmar surfaces of the lunate and triquetrum, and the ulnar collateral band from the styloid to the triquetrum and pisiform. MEASURED (probe_palm.py). 20 Oct: the UCL finish (owner) - fine fibres, one per ridge of grain, rendered with --ao. 20 Oct 2026: exactCount, so the gap-filling never lays fibres between bundles through the carpal bones (owner: phased through).

ulnar-collateral-ligament._why: UCL as its anterior band (medial epicondyle to the coronoid process) and posterior band (to the medial olecranon), as on the owner's slide. Added 20 Oct 2026 from the elbow slides (elbow deck p8-p15). MEASURED (probe_elbow.py, left elbow, world mm: +x lateral, +y posterior): medial epicondyle (183.5,35.6,1107), lateral epicondyle (248.8,43.3,1112.8), coronoid (218,22.5,1091.2), olecranon medial edge (203.2,52,1098.3), radial head centre (238.1,29,1087.9) radius 13.2mm, top z 1093.3, radial notch (226.3,28.6,1084.4). SECOND PASS (owner's diagram, 20 Oct): three bundles - anterior (medial epicondyle to the coronoid process), posterior (a fan from the epicondyle to the medial olecranon) and transverse (along the ulna from the coronoid to the olecranon). THIRD PASS (owner: combine the broad sheet with the separate parts): the broad continuous spans again, drawn as individual fibres with no remeshing, so each bundle's fibre direction shows where the bundles meet. FOURTH PASS (owner: merge the two looks). Each bundle a smooth solid band (the broad render) with fine fibre lines laid along its surface (the fibred render); the three bands kept apart. The fibre lines (grainBuild) sit on the bands' surface in a darker cyan. FIFTH PASS (owner's reference image, straight medial view): one broad continuous fan from the medial epicondyle spreading over the ulna from the coronoid to the olecranon, with the transverse band along its base, solid with a fibre grain. SIXTH PASS (owner: why are the grains like that?): the separate grain cords dipped in and out of the band; the grain is now the band's own surface - overlapping fibres remeshed finely and only lightly smoothed, so each fibre leaves a shallow ridge. SEVENTH PASS (owner: grain must match the fibres, bone-level realism): finer fibres (0.75mm, 52 across the fan, 24 in the transverse band) so every ridge is one fibre, and rendered with ambient occlusion (--ao) like the bone.
